newsitem.title: JORDAN: Arab Bank pulls Jordan stocks lower.
newsitem.headline: Arab Bank pulls Jordan stocks lower.

text.p: Poor demand for market leader Arab Bank dragged the Amman stock exchange down at the end of weekly trade on Wednesday despite some speculative interest in key shares, dealers said.

The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index dropped 1.02 percent to below the psychological 150-point barrier, ending the day on 149.49 points after heavy trade worth 1.8 million dinars ($2.54 million).
The market started its rise to four month highs last week as optimism over goverment commitment to economic reform and a healthy batch of half year results pushed blue-chip shares up.

Heavyweight Arab Bank, which drove the index upwards in the first half of September, shed four dinars on Tuesday to 241 dinars as investors sold to cash in on its recent highs in trade worth 276,490 dinars.
"The heavy buying orders on Arab Bank have stopped and those who bought the shares at below 240 were sellers," one broker said.
Brokers fear the market may be running out of steam as institutional investors continue to wait in the sidelines and profit-takers eat into the recent gains.
But Livestock and Poultry, focus of investor interest for the third week in a row, rose to 0.83 dinars and continued to dominate trade with a 490,908 dinar turnover.
Healthy demand on Housing Bank pushed the stock 50 fils to 5.04 dinars with 85,555 shares changing hands.
Brokers suspect major shareholders bought and sold the company in speculative trade aimed at nudging the price up.
Of 48 stocks traded, 24 fell, 12 advanced, and 12 closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange fell 0.13 percent to 82.60 points, still 13.52 percent down from the same time last year.
